newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians say Israelis made them drink urine.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians say Israelis made them drink urine.

text.p: Palestinian teenagers on Wednesday charged that Israeli soldiers made them drink urine during a brief detention in the West Bank town of Hebron two days earlier.

Bahjat Abdel-Raaouf al-Awaiwi, 16 and Abdel-Raouf al-Awaiwi, 14, in a complaint filed with the Arab municipality of Hebron said that Israeli soldiers on Monday detained them along with 28 other Palestinians and held them at a military checkpoint in central Hebron while the city was under curfew.
"When we asked for water, the soldiers brought us bottles of stinking yellow liquid. We refused to drink when we found that it smelled like urine," Bahjat said in the complaint.
"The soldiers beat us and forced us to drink from the bottles," he added.
Officials at the municipality conveyed the complaint to the Israeli military authorities who in turn referred them to the local police.
A spokesman for international monitors in Hebron said the Hebron municipality informed him of the complaint and was sending him a copy.
An Israeli army spokesman said he was checking the report.

Hebron, the only West bank city yet to be handed to the PLO under a self-rule deal signed last year, was under curfew during clashes and gun battles last week in which 57 Palestinians and 15 Israelis were killed. The curfew is still in force.
